Anatomy Reference

Each wolf's pelt is encoded across 9 regions, grouped into 4 anatomical zones. Codes within a region capture the morphological variation noted in the rightmost column. Click a region row to highlight it in the schematic.

Per-Region Identification Breakdown — Version A · Discrete Buckets

Each column represents one region. Each bar holds 100% of the analysed wolves (n = 0), partitioned into identification-power buckets: Unique = wolves whose code in this region appears in no other wolf; Shared 2-3 → 36+ = a heat-map of how widely a code is reused (lighter = uncommon, darker brown = dominates the population); Asymmetric / Partial / P / N = non-resolvable categories. Hover any segment for exact counts. Use Plotly's camera icon to download as PNG.

Per-Region Identification Breakdown

Each column represents one region; each bar holds 100% of the analysed wolves (n = 0). Unique = wolves whose code in this region appears in no other wolf. The Shared portion — every band above the dark-green Unique base — is a continuous heat-map: each band is coloured by the exact number of wolves that share that code (darkest green = shared by few, palest green = shared by many), and the colour bar on the right maps shade to share-count. Asymmetric = wolf carries a different code on its right vs. left side; Partial = code is a substring of another code or has a missing character; P = a fur marking is visible but too indistinct to assign a code (the presence itself is informative — we know something is there); N = no codable view — either the region was never captured in any photo, or it was captured but too poorly (angle, lighting, blur) to read anything from. Segments ≥10% are labelled with their percentage; hover any segment for exact counts. Use Plotly's camera icon to download as PNG.

Per-Region Identification Breakdown — Edited Copy For Comparison

Same data and same heat-map as the chart above. Three visual edits to compare against the original: (1) N is rendered black instead of red; (2) P is rendered a medium-dark grey (darker than Partial-Ambiguous, lighter than N); (3) Asymmetric is folded into the dark-green Unique (1) segment instead of getting its own band.

Single-Region Power — Bars Sorted by ID Power

For each region alone (k=1), how many wolves get a unique fingerprint? Bar colour follows the anatomical group.

Social Dynamics — Where the Wolves Live and How They Group

Camera-survey pool only  ·  ? wolves analysed . Three views: spatial (which polygon), structural (which pack), and behavioural (pack / group / lone / unknown). Wolves marked with * are probable, not certain.

1. Overall Social-Dynamic Mix — Probables Separated

All analysed (camera-survey) wolves, by canonical social category. Leader-line callouts point from each hatched wedge to its probable (*) count and its share of the pool.

1. Overall Social-Dynamic Mix

All analysed (camera-survey) wolves, by canonical social category. Each probable (*) wolf is folded into the social category it is assigned to (pack / group / lone); the wedge label notes how many of its wolves are probable, and the hover tooltip gives the full confirmed / probable breakdown.

2. Land-Use Class — Wolves per Category, Stacked by Social

Polygons grouped by land-use class (per the paper's key). Nature Reserve = Yehudiya + Odem (most protected). Minefield = Makhfi + Saki + Hazeka (no humans). High Culling = Shaal + Snir + Keshet-Yonatan. Low Culling = Slopes + Firing-Zone + Masade.

3. Pack Inventory — Sizes and Home Polygons

Each row is one identified pack. Land-use chip shows the class of the pack's home polygon (blue=Nature Reserve, orange=Minefield, pink=High Culling, green=Low Culling). Sentinels (lone / no-pack / indeterminate) sit below the divider in muted grey.

4. Per-Polygon Stacked by Social Dynamic

Each polygon's bar shows how its wolves split among pack / group / lone / unknown. Polygon name colour = land-use class. Hover for breakdown.

Pack Signatures — What Unites and Individualises Within Each Pack

Each named pack (n ≥ 2): the pattern axis tends to individualise members; the colour and contrast axes tend to tag the pack. Each region is split by its grammar — A1/A2/C6/D8 → pattern + colour; B3/B4/B5 → pattern + a/b contrast; D9 → contrast level only; C7 → pattern only.

Cross-Pack Colour Signatures

Per pack × per colour-bearing region: the most-common colour in that pack (large), its share, and 1–2 secondary colours. When multiple colours tie for the top count, the cell is split into one strip per tied colour. Cell background uses each region's reference palette (bubble shades from the colour-code maps).

Top 3 Packs per Region — Colour / Contrast Comparison

For each region: the three packs whose colour (A1/A2/C6/D8), contrast (B3/B4/B5/D9), or pattern (C7) is most consistent within the pack. Each vertical bar shows one pack's full within-pack distribution at the region's primary axis; the diagonal-striped grey segment marks wolves without info on this axis (N/P or code missing the relevant half), so each bar represents the whole pack. Packs with fewer than 3 observed wolves on that region are excluded so small-sample 100%s don't dominate.

Region-Role Map

Average within-pack modal % per region per axis. High → the axis consistently tags the pack; low → the axis individualises wolves.

Pack Profile Cards — Per-Region Breakdown

Each card shows one pack. Bars are full within-pack distributions (sorted by frequency). Region rows tinted green = all members share an identical code.

About this page: Read-only by default. The Admin login (password protected) lets the data owner edit cells in the browser. Edits don't change the file on the server — clicking Save downloads an updated wolves_data.xlsx which the owner places back in the project folder. Running update.bat then refreshes all analyses and rebuilds this page.
Security note: the admin password is a soft client-side gate. It prevents accidental edits, not determined viewers. All data on this page is visible to anyone who can open it (this is by design — the table is meant to be shared).
